pairs.subject: scale-investment-timing
pairs.evidence: src/api/system/tierUsage.ts:9 The context is a set of pass-through Tauri IPC wrappers (tier/rate-bucket usage, host metrics, cloud, design, templates) that read limits and load computed in the Rust backend and size nothing themselves; a search of the context's files and of all of src/api for shard, runway, horizontal, replica and vertical returned zero hits, and the only 'ceiling'/'limit'/'worker' hits are an IPC timeout bound, list pagination and a re-exported cloud binding type, so no capacity ceiling, sizing axis, distribution choice, execution-model adoption or growth-driven migration is decided here.

techniques.evidence: src/api/templates/templateAdopt.ts:60 The only 'ceiling' in the context is a CLI-runner timeout bound mirrored into the IPC timeout, not a capacity ceiling for an architecture; no load ceiling is stated or owned here.
src/api/system/systemMetrics.ts:12 Host CPU/memory are only read for a footer gauge; the wrappers pick no execution or flow-control model, which lives in the Rust runtime.
src/api/templates/templateAdopt.ts:18 The only change history recorded here is the removal of dead wrappers, not a platform migration proposed on growth grounds.
src/api/templates/n8nTransform.ts:320 The numeric limits in the context are pagination defaults for list reads, not a design sized against a named load axis.
